# FIBOM-AI: Artificial Intelligence-based Prediction of BOne Marrow FIBrosis

**FIB**rosis in **BO**ne **M**arrow Prediction using AI

DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A MACHINE-LEARNING MODEL TO PREDICT BONE MARROW FIBROSIS FROM COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT IN MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS (FIBOM-AI): A MULTICENTRE STUDY

Lancet Haematology, 2026, xxxx

**Methods**

Histopathological and CBC data from 1,995 patients undergoing bone marrow biopsies between Jan 1, 2014 and December 31, 2023 were retrospectively collected across 13 French university hospitals. Biopsies were performed either at diagnosis or during follow-up for suspected or established MPNs. Twenty-seven CBC variables and patient age at biopsy were used as predictors. Data from six independent centres were used for model development and the remaining seven centres were used for external validation. The primary outcome was grade 2-3 fibrosis as a binary endpoint. Nine algorithms were trained using 10-fold cross validation. The final model was evaluated in a real-life prospective setting on all bone marrow biopsies performed between January 1, 2024 and December 31, 2024 in 4 French centres and 1 Canadian centre (n=493 biopsies).

The XGBoost model achieved the best performances with an AUC [95% CI] of 0.96 [0.95-0.97], 0.90 [0.85-0.95], and 0.92 [0.90-0.95] on the training, testing, and validation sets. Clinical cutoffs to guide decision were set, leading to a final accuracy of 88.1%, 87.0%, and 88.6% for the overall predictions and 99%, 95%, and 97% for the confident predictions in the training, testing, and validation sets, respectively. Prospective evaluation showed an accuracy of 85.2% (range: 82-87%) for the overall predictions and 98.6% (range: 96-100%) for the confident predictions. 

FIBOM-AI can be reliably used as a triage and prioritisation tool to support timely bone marrow evaluation or provide complementary risk assessment when bone marrow biopsy is not immediately feasible. 


# Getting started

FIBOM-AI is a free and open-source software package built in R, with a user-friendly interface provided via Shiny, that enables clinical hematologists and biologists to predict grade 2-3 bone marrow fibrosis based solely on complete blood count.


## Online version 

FIBOM-AI has a ready-to-use online version available at [https://alcazerv.shinyapps.io/FIBOM-AI/](https://alcazerv.shinyapps.io/FIBOM-AI/).

## Local version

You can install a local version from [GitHub](https://github.com/VincentAlcazer/FIBOM-AI) either by cloning the repository or directly by downloading the package in R:
You'll need to have R (>= 4.1.0) and the remotes package installed.

```{r Github install, eval = F }

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("VincentAlcazer/FIBOM-AI")

FIBOMAI::run_app()
```

The FIBOM-AI Shiny app will open in your default web browser.
